summary: Jan Peter F. Hintelmann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper. He also studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Pieter Hogendijk studied at Utrecht University (~1974–1983) and under G. J. Toomer (~1983–1985). He held posts at Brown, Frankfurt, Heidelberg, Utrecht (including Professor of History of Mathematics, 2005), Leiden (2004–2009), King Fahd University (~2004), and University of Tehran (2008–2010).

Jan Westerhoff studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, earned a PhD at Cambridge under Michael Potter (~1999–2003), and another PhD at SOAS (~2003–2007). He held posts at CUNY, Columbia, Linacre College, SOAS, Durham, and became Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Oxford (~2013).

Jan Willem de Jong studied at Leiden (PhD), Sorbonne, and Collège de France under F. B. J. Kuiper, Paul Demiéville, and Walter Eugene Clark. He held chairs at Leiden (1950–1956) and the Australian National University (1965–1986).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. He held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, Hamburg, Munich, and served as professor at the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006).

Jane Bunnag is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London by 1969, where she studied under supervisors E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College, Newnham College, and under Robert Alexander Neil (~1876–1880). She held a post at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1898 to 1922.

Janet Gyatso studied at UC Berkeley (BA, MA, PhD 1981). A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religion, she held posts at Stony Brook, Wesleyan, Amherst College (1987–2001), and Harvard University as Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies from 2001.
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis studied at Cornell and Columbia (PhD ~1976) under Alex Wayman and Lama Thubten Yeshe. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, she was a professor at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and taught at Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Khenpo Sonam Tenpa. He also held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 2007).

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 41st Sakya Trizin and completed his dissertation at Columbia University by 1985 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Jarl Charpentier studied Indology and linguistics at Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He served as Assistant Professor at Uppsala from 1908 and succeeded Johansson in 1927.
Jaroslav Průšek was a scholar of Sinology who studied at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts from around 1924 to 1928, and later taught Karel Werner.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney and earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019). He held the Theiline Pigott McCone Chair in Humanities at Seattle University from 2014 to 2016.

Jason Matthew McCombs, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at the University of Michigan and earned his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen by 2014. He also served as a lecturer at UCLA (attested 2014).

Jason Neelis studied at UT Austin and the University of Washington (PhD 2001) under Richard Salomon. He held posts at the University of Washington, Käte Hamburger Kolleg (2009–2010), and Wilfrid Laurier University as Associate Professor and Chair (attested 2013–2021).

Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016). He held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Jay Holt Valentine is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer and David Germano.
